title: Topology- and Geometry-Exact Discretizations for Fluid–Structure Interaction (Jonathan Panuelos, U. of Toronto)
description: Topology- and Geometry-Exact Discretizations for Fluid–Structure Interaction (Jonathan Panuelos, U. of Toronto) Abstract:  A parachute is a hundred microns of fabric travelling through a much larger volume of fluid. A heart valve consists of two leaflets that must meet and form a watertight seal. In problems like these, the geometry of the solid alone decides which paths a fluid can take, and resolving this exactly should be as important to our simulators as conservation laws and invariants.This talk will argue for discretizations that preserve the local flow topology, showing that retaining the proper connectivity of the fluid domain resolves errors in numerical sealing and leaking, independent of resolution. I will introduce a Lagrangian Voronoi partitioning scheme clipped and stitched against the solid to retain the correct fluid adjacencies, applied to both incompressible and compressible fluids. From this, I will demonstrate the key geometric requirements satisfied by the mesh, and extract only those and remove everything else to recover a meshless discretization that behaves much closer to their meshed counterparts than current methods. title: Instance-optimal estimation of L2-norm
description: Instance-optimal estimation of L2-norm Abstract: The $L_2$-norm, or collision norm, is a core entity in the analysis of distributions and probabilistic algorithms. Batu and Canonne (FOCS 2017) presented an extensive analysis of algorithmic aspects of the $L_2$-norm and its connection to uniformity testing. However, when it comes to estimating the $L_2$-norm itself, their algorithm is not always optimal compared to the instance-specific second-moment bounds, $O(1/(\varepsilon\|\mu\|_2) + t_\mu/\varepsilon^2)$, for $t_\mu = \|\mu\|_3^3 / \|\mu\|_2^4 - 1$, as stated by Batu (WoLA 2025, open problem session).In this paper, we present an unbiased $L_2$-estimation algorithm whose sample complexity matches the instance-specific second-moment analysis. Additionally, we show that $\Omega(1/(\varepsilon \|\mu\|_2) + t_\mu / \varepsilon^2)$ is indeed the per-instance lower bound for estimating the norm of a distribution $\mu$ by sampling (even for non-unbiased estimators). title: Recent Results in Graph Property Testing via the Container Method
description: Recent Results in Graph Property Testing via the Container Method Abstract: Recent work has shown that the graph container method is a useful tool for analyzing property testing algorithms for a number of classic properties including k-colorability, rho-clique and satisfiability. In this talk we will demonstrate that there is a deeper connection between the container method and graph property testing. For hereditary properties, we relate one-sided testability to the existence of a type of container lemma, and we obtain quantitative bounds in both directions. As applications, we obtain closure results for partition properties and new testing results for graph and digraph properties such as the dichromatic number.  TBD August 17, 2026 Diagnosing and Managing Performance in Data Systems Markos Markakis MIT CSAIL Part Of Thesis Defense 1:00 P - 2:00 P Location 32-G882
